attestations.note: The identification is exact and the Russian is far fuller than the source this folder was made from: the line gives the see of Kherson and the year 1857 the folder already holds, and the life, life4817, opens «Святитель Иннокентий, архиепископ Херсонский и Таврический (в миру Иван Алексеевич Борисов) родился 15 декабря 1800 года в городе Ельце Орловской губернии в семье священника Успенской церкви Алексия Борисова» — the same full date of birth, the same town and the same priestly family the folder’s existing `dates` cite from saint.gr. `dates` is unchanged. WHAT THE RUSSIAN ADDS TO THE DEATH IS THE DAY AND THE PLACE: «на обратном пути в Одессу скончался в Херсоне 25 мая 1857 года в светлый праздник Живоначальной Троицы» — at Kherson, on this feast’s own day, on Trinity Sunday; the schema’s interval carries years only, so it is in the life. `archbishop` WAS ADDED to the folder’s lone `hierarch`, off the line’s own «архиеп.» and the name link’s «архиепископ Херсонский и Таврический», and `office` SET TO «Archbishop», a word the four locale packs carry and thirteen folders already use; the see is NOT in the office, per BRIEF-ADDENDUM §4. The life page lists no day but this one, and the calendar records the canonisation: «Канонизован Русской Православной Церковью в 1997 году». azbyka.ru was not read.

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 25 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar keeps «Sfântul Inochentie al Odessei» on, and the identification is the see: saint.gr calls him bishop of Kherson, and Kherson and all Taurida was the diocese seated at Odessa, which the folder's Romanian line names him by. The Greek adds a whole life the Romanian line does not carry — the name in the world, the parents, the schools, the successive sees and the Crimean War. He is not the corpus's `innocent-of-moscow`. **The folder's `dates` is left empty for the writer to fill or leave**: the page gives «γεννήθηκε στις 15 Δεκεμβρίου 1800 μ.Χ.» and «κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη το 1857 μ.Χ.», both flat and both repeated in its head line «(1800 - 1857)», so these are recordable years — but a reader does not replace a folder's `dates` from an upgrade file in this wave, and the years are set down here and in the added paragraph instead. Its `types` are also short of the Greek: the folder says `hierarch`, and the page says bishop of Chigirin, then Vologda, then Kharkov, then Kherson. No hymn is printed.
